title: Chapter 3256 City of Gates
content:
The houses had all been destroyed, but Sunny's old home was quite special. Even if everything above the ground did not exist anymore, there was still his underground bunker — the place where he and Nephis had trained Rain in swordsmanship, and where his sleeping pod used to stand.

It took Rain no more than a few minutes to identify the correct location amidst the rubble, then a few more to clear the debris away and tear apart the armored doors of the elevator shaft.

Then, she carried Tamar down into the lightless, quiet safety of the fortified bunker.

It was warm there — the ground still radiated the heat after fire rolled through the district — and, most importantly, dry. The darkness did not prevent either of them from seeing clearly, so Rain pried the sleeping pod open and put Tamar inside instead of lowering her to the floor.

Tamar let out a pained grunt, then took a few labored breaths, a stark pallor draining her face of color.

Rain froze for a moment when a subtle tremor of a distant impact shook the bunker. Once it passed, she spent some time studying Tamar's wounds.

“How do you feel?"

Tamar stared at the ceiling, finally allowing herself to relax. After a short stretch of silence, she said neutrally:

"Nothing to worry about. A bit of rest, and I'll be as good as new."

Rain tended to disagree. This time, her friend had gotten hurt too badly — it was going to take a while, a week at least, for her to recover enough to move freely... and even longer before she was back to her top shape.

But at least the wounds did not look fatal. Recovery was only a matter of time — which was a good thing, considering that Rain was not sure that they would be able to fight their way to a healer.

‘I wonder how Fleur is doing.'

Healers had always been a rarity, and now, with field hospitals splitting at the seams from the constant influx of wounded soldiers, their services were even more difficult to come by. Rain and Tamar were now behind enemy lines, cut off from reinforcements, and they could not even use the Dream Realm to escape their predicament.

That was because the Call was too powerful in NQSC, the influence of countless Nightmare Gates overlapping to create an almost impenetrable barrier.

Once there were no unaffected areas left at all...

The experience of the past two years suggested that another Category Five Gate would shatter the sky above the city. Effie and Kai were already preparing to face the Cursed Ones that would use it to enter the waking world, but in the meantime, the battle for NQSC was growing more and more bitter with each day.

Most civilians had already been evacuated to the Dream Realm, leaving the city an empty shell of its former self. But the soldiers still defended it with suicidal fervor, refusing to let the Nightmare Creatures conquer the former capital of humanity.

In part, it was because of what NQSC represented.

But mostly, it was because NQSC could not be allowed to fall.

Humanity needed to keep at least a piece of the waking world intact. So, cohorts of Awakened and Ascended were brought here every day, sent to challenge the Nightmare Gates and, hopefully, close them — postponing the day NQSC would become a part of the Dream Realm, even if only by a little bit.

They needed to do it, because that was the will of the Supremes.

And the Supremes had come to the heavy decision to keep NQSC out of the Dream Realm's jaws at all costs after a long and difficult deliberation.

Their reasoning was simple — the moment the last piece of the waking world was consumed, Earth's moon would shine above the Dream Realm. Once it did, the creature imprisoned on it would no longer be bound by the laws of the Dream Realm... and among all the fallen deities born out of the Nightmare, the one who could gaze upon all of humanity from up high was the most calamitous.

So, above all else, one piece of the waking world had to be preserved until the four Supremes who had challenged the Fifth Nightmare returned as Spirits — so that they could launch an attack on the Moon before the being hidden there descended from the night sky.

So that they could challenge the Sixth Nightmare and become gods before humanity was no more.

That was why Rain and Tamar were still in NQSC, and why human soldiers were fighting for it even now that there were no civilians left in the ruins, and it had become a city of Nightmare Gates instead of a city of humans.

All of existence was drowning in the throes of battle... but these ruins were destined to become the final battlefield of the last war. Sitting down and leaning against a wall, Rain looked around, remembering the carefree days of her distant youth.

The underground dojo was dry and safe, but it was also barren and empty. Still, Rain remembered the past fondly.

A few moments later, she said:

"I guess we are stuck here for a while, aren't we?"

She could use Memories and sorcery to contact agents of the Shadow Clan scattered across the city... if that was not enough, she could even contact Aiko.

Revel and most of the Shadow Clan's forces were engaged in a harrowing battle against the Barrow Wraiths and the thing that had emerged from the depths of the Burned Forest, but they would still send someone to fight through the mass of abominations here and extract Lady of Sorrow and the Princess of Shadows.

However, what was the point?

It was not like the Shadow Clan had many fighters on Tamar's and Rain's level — definitely not those whom Revel could spare. A straining rescue mission when the target was not even in immediate danger sounded like a waste of resources. In the worst case, the rescuers would perish on the way or end up trapped, as well.

So, the best thing Rain and Tamar could do was hunker down in Sunny's old basement until the latter recovered, and then try their luck outside.

“Do you feel very lucky?"

Tamar's question stumped Rain. Looking at her friends, she made a grimace.

“Since when did you develop an Ability to read my thoughts?"

Tamar chuckled, then groaned quietly when that easy motion disturbed her wounds.

“Please. You're so obvious."

She remained silent for a while, then asked in a subdued tone:

“How far are you from breaking through to Transcendence?"

Rain studied Tamar somberly.

Eventually, she sighed and leaned back.

“Transcendence? Child's play. If I focus, I can probably get it over in a couple weeks."

Tamar smiled, then closed her eyes tiredly. "Good. Do that, then — I don't think we'll be able to escape this one alive unless you become a Saint. So..."

She inhaled deeply.

“Wake me up when you do."

With that, Tamar fell quiet.

Rain turned to her worriedly, then rose to look inside the sleeping pod.

"Hey! Why... why are you quiet all of a sudden?"

A moment later, her face froze.

Rain stared into the sleeping pod motionlessly for a few moments, then spoke quietly:

"This wench."

The sound of soft snores reached her ears.

"She really is asleep!"

Scoffing in disbelief, Rain returned to her spot by the wall and stared into the darkness.

‘Why sleeps so peacefully when the world is ending?’

She smiled and shook her head.

'Transcendence. Sure... why not? Let's give it a try.'

With that, she closed her eyes as well.

Only, unlike Tamar, she did not close them to sleep.

The seventh year of apocalypse was approaching swiftly.
